summary: The note curator's merge-group evidence exemption no longer follows a note into an individual retirement its group's merge never actually offered — closing/expiring/mooting a note now needs real evidence unless it is genuinely part of an accepted merge this tick.
details: Found by adversarial review after issue #100 gave `note_entity` a writer and made merge groups reachable in production. `_ground`'s exemption previously keyed on CANDIDATE-group membership (`note_id not in shown.due_or_anchored`, true of every member of every colliding group, offered or not) rather than on whether the group's merge was actually offered/accepted this tick. That was safe only as long as `merge_groups` always returned empty (pre-#100); once groups became reachable, a model returning an individual `closed`/`moot`/`expired` verdict for a note whose group's merge was declined (no `merged_body` this tick) retired it via `supersede` with zero citation or evidence grounding -- the one path where this tier's 'silence is not an answer' guarantee was silently bypassed.

Fix: `nora/language/note_curator.py`'s `_ground` and `commit` now derive the exemption from a single shared function, `_merged_away_ids` -- every note id belonging to a group whose SURVIVOR was named with a `merged_body` this tick, the same set `commit`'s own `untouchable` already used to guard against piecemeal retirement of a failed merge. A group member whose merge was not offered this tick falls into the ordinary evidence-grounded path any other note takes.
limitations: `inputs` still never gathers evidence for a merge-group member (unchanged, deliberately -- a per-candidate `RecordStore.recent` read for a path that was inert until #100 was rejected as unrelated scope creep). So a note whose merge is declined and not offered again falls back to a real evidence check that always finds none, and is refused `no_evidence` rather than ever retiring on that path -- correctly fail-closed, but it means such a note can only leave its group by actually merging or by the group ceasing to collide, not by an individual verdict, until a future change gives group members a real evidence read.
Not reachable in the current deployment: `[notes] curator_enabled = false`, so no merge or retirement runs today regardless of this fix.
